syllabusTopics: Solving first order, first degree equations: variable separable, homogeneous, linear
Applications: growth and decay, population dynamics
agentNotes: Authoring contract: frontend/AGENTS.md §9. Filled 2026-10-06 (Class 12 track); no Class-12 PYQ bank in-corpus, so the board row is NEB-style with no fabricated citation.

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Differential equations model change itself: form them by eliminating arbitrary constants (one constant → differentiate once), then solve by type — separable (split x/y sides and integrate), homogeneous (y = vx substitution homogenises degree), linear (dy/dx + Py = Q via integrating factor e^∫Pdx). Growth/decay and population dynamics are the flagship applications (exponential solutions).

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: formation: differentiate n times to kill n constants  ·  separable: dy/dx = f(x)g(y) → ∫dy/g = ∫fdx  ·  homogeneous: y = vx → separable in v,x  ·  linear: IF = e^∫Pdx; y·IF = ∫Q·IF·dx + C  ·  growth: dN/dt = kN → N = N₀e^(kt)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Order/degree read after clearing radicals/fractions (degree undefined otherwise). Separable needs factorable form; homogeneous needs same-degree M/N; linear needs first-degree in y (Bernoulli yⁿ generalises with z = y^(1−n)). Solutions need the constant C fixed by given conditions.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Family of circles x² + y² = a² → differentiate: 2x + 2yy′ = 0 → x + yy′ = 0 (one constant, first order). Population doubling drills: N = N₀e^(kt) with k from doubling time. Orthogonal trajectories: replace y′ with −1/y′ and solve again.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Solve dy/dx + y·tan x = sec x: linear with P = tan x → IF = e^∫tan x dx = e^(−ln cos x) = sec x. Then y·sec x = ∫sec²x dx = tan x + C → y = sin x + C·cos x. Template: IF → multiply → integrate → divide.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Only first-order first-degree types are in syllabus — higher orders need new machinery (auxiliary equations). Formation by elimination can introduce singular solutions the family never shows. Linear IF method fails nonlinear-in-y equations (Riccati and friends).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Linear derivation: multiply dy/dx + Py = Q by IF = e^∫Pdx → left side collapses to d(y·IF)/dx (product rule in reverse) → integrate directly. Formation: n constants need n differentiations, then eliminate — the equation's order equals the constants killed.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Type radar: separable? split and integrate. Same-degree M/N? y = vx. y′ + Py = Q shape? Integrating factor immediately. Formation: count constants (= order), differentiate that many times, eliminate.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: formation from curve families; one separable, one homogeneous, one linear solution; growth/decay and population word problems to exponential form.
